title: Hierarchical failover throttle with session-preserving circuit and SLO-aware shedding
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Hosted API gateways sometimes experience region-wide capacity spikes where naive full-shift failover causes streaming session disruption, KV cache divergence, and SLO violations on the target region. We need a deterministic, observable, and reversible approach that: (1) protects p99 latency and error-budget targets, (2) preserves in-flight streaming/session continuity where possible, and (3) gracefully sheds non-critical traffic in an SLO-aware manner instead of bluntly draining all requests.

Goal:
Design and implement a hierarchical failover throttle that orchestrates incremental traffic attenuation ("thinning") across egress tiers, integrates a session-preserving circuit for streaming handoffs, and triggers SLO-aware load-shedding policies before full cross-region shifts. The system should be conservative by default and have clear runbooks for emergency full-shift.

Summary of approach:
1) Hierarchical throttle: define traffic attenuation at three levels — edge proxy weights, regional gateway ingress, and per-model serving pools. A centralized controller computes target weights using SLO consumption signals and capacity estimates and applies staged adjustments with a soft ramp (configurable step sizes and hold windows).
2) Session-preserving circuit: for streaming sessions, establish a lightweight continuity token and checkpoint handshake so a session can be resumed on the target region without replaying the full context or corrupting KV caches. For incompatible models, the circuit falls back to a degraded-but-consistent short-response mode (end-of-stream marker + user-visible retry guidance).
3) SLO-aware shedding: define shedding policies tied to specific SLO thresholds (e.g., error budget burn > 8% in 10m triggers client-tier thinning; >20% triggers model-tier shedding). Shedding should be deterministic and observable: prefer stateless, idempotent requests first, then best-effort cacheable traffic.
4) Telemetry and decision engine: augment our control plane with new derived signals (moving-window error-budget burn, regional tail-latency anomaly score, KV-sync lag) and a simulation sandbox to evaluate weight changes before applying them in production.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can apply staged weight changes at edge, gateway, and model pool tiers with configurable step and hold parameters
99th percentile downstream latency remains within configured SLO during controlled thinning exercises in staging
Streaming sessions that opt-in to continuity tokens can resume in the target region with no more than a single soft-retry
Load-shedding rules can be triggered automatically by derived SLO signals and are reversible within configured windows
New dashboards surface weight-change events, projected SLO impact, and rollback guidance
steps: Design API for hierarchical-weight controller and policy DSL (edge,gateway,pool)
Implement controller with dry-run/simulate mode and compare against real traffic in canary
Add continuity token circuit to edge proxy and gateway handshake for streaming sessions
Implement KV sync snapshot endpoints to speed session resume on target region
Add SLO-derived signals in metrics pipeline and unit tests for threshold behavior
Create observability dashboards and alerting for weight changes, rollbacks, and shedding activations
Run staged chaos exercises in pre-prod (gradual attenuation, forced region pressure) to validate runbook
telemetry_changes: Derived: slo_pressure_score (composite of burn, p99_delta, kv_sync_lag)
Tracing: continuity-token-handshake span and resume-latency histogram
Event: shedding.activation with reason, scope, and projected impact
rollout_plan: Phase A (staging): enable controller in simulate mode and run synthetic pressure tests to validate metric correlations; Phase B (canary): enable soft-apply for a single low-traffic region and verify rollback behavior; Phase C (regional pilot): allow auto-thinning for non-critical routes with continuity token opt-in; Phase D (global): enable for all tenants with default conservative thresholds and operator override. Each phase has a 72h observation window and automated rollback hooks if slo_pressure_score exceeds safe threshold.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Avery Chen: Created ticket. Initial design workshop notes attached to attachments. Identified key unknowns: continuity-token size, KV snapshot frequency, and per-tenant shedding policies.

2026-03-07 - Liam O'Neill: Spike complete for controller simulate mode. Simulate results show weight changes with step <= 10% and hold >= 30s produce stable p95 in staging. Uploaded simulation graphs to attachments.

2026-03-09 - Nikhil Rao (SRE): Proposed two-tier continuity token: lightweight pointer for recent KV-prefixed state, full checkpoint fallback for long-lived sessions. Concerned about token replay attack surface; recommend short TTL and signing with KMS.
2026-03-10 - Design review (Priya Kumar): UX needs explicit client opt-in for continuity token; add docs to SDK about resume semantics and error codes when graceful handoff isn't possible.

2026-03-12 - Security (Marta Silva): Recommended HSM-signed continuity tokens and audit log entries for all cross-region resume events. Flagging security_review_required=false in ticket but will file a separate security checklist PR.
